newsitem.title: USA: WSCC confident of 6,250 MW Intertie through April.
newsitem.headline: WSCC confident of 6,250 MW Intertie through April.

text.p: A Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) study group convened to review Pacific Intertie operations, is "confident" that the recent increase to 6,250 megawatts will remain in place at least through April, the group's chairman said this week.
Bob Stuart, chairman of the technical study group, said contingency studies indicate "the winter plan could carry us through" to it's expiration on April 30.
Other industry sources have been concerned that the 6,250 MW level could revert back to 5,200 MW if system conditions shift from "winter" to "spring" before the end of April.
But Stuart said typical spring changes--such as high runoff in the Columbia River basin--improve rather than degrade the transmission system's reliability.
He explained that the stresses on the system become alarming when bypass flows are high and demand in California is high, events which typically do not occur until summer.
"I am confident that if we have increased lower Columbia generation and lower loads in the Northwest it is only a plus," Stuart said.

But he noted recent concerns raised by Arizona utilities regarding a further increase in the Intertie capacity have complicated efforts to come up with a spring operating plan acceptable to all WSCC members.

The Arizona utilities are asking that California utilities implement a system of direct load tripping so that the Desert Southwest is shielded from the type of cascading blackouts which hit the West last summer.
"They don't want to expose their customers. Their commissions have hammered them pretty hard," said Stuart.

He remains convinced that there is "plenty of margin" in the transmission system to allow for the worst-case contingencies, but said the issue may need to be ironed out before a spring capacity rate is settled.
The WSCC study group is expected to submit a final report, which would include a variety of options for raising the limit to above 7,000 MW, to the council's board early next month.
